text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.1% today to $134.26, pulling back from yesterday's high of $137.20 after a week of gains. The decline came as crude oil prices softened slightly (US oil at $91.48/barrel, down from recent strength), and broader geopolitical tensions—while supportive of energy prices overall—appear to have created some uncertainty. Yesterday's diesel shortage story, driven by damaged refineries in Ukraine and Russia, had boosted the stock, but today's pullback suggests that short-term trade momentum reversed as the market digested those moves.

The longer-running backdrop remains mixed for oil majors: conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East are disrupting refinery capacity and shipping routes (potentially supporting prices and refining margins), but Trump's newly announced Venezuela oil deal and the push toward geothermal alternatives hint at shifting energy policy that could reshape oil demand. Over two weeks, ConocoPhillips has been essentially flat, caught between these countervailing pressures.
